topics.name: event grain (base_events)
topics.subject: valorant
skills: Recognize that one row of base_events = one event (kill / plant / defuse / ability)
Events must carry a round_id before they can be rolled up into round-level statistics

examples.prompt: How many types of events happened in this match, and how many of each?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain first: the question asks about events, not rounds → use base_events.
MCP: get_database_info() —— confirm the table name and row count, don't guess.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT event_type, COUNT(*) FROM base_events WHERE round_id IN (SELECT round_id FROM rounds WHERE series_id = ?) GROUP BY event_type")
When reporting the count you must state that this is an event count, which is not the same as the round count.

typical_misconceptions: Treating base_events as the round table and running COUNT(*) on it directly —— one round contains a dozen or more events, so what you count is events, not rounds

topics.name: round grain (rounds)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Rounds are aggregated from events; without knowing what an event looks like you cannot pin down the definition of a round win

skills: One row of rounds = one round, carrying round_number / map_name / winning_team_name
Always count rounds with COUNT(*), never with SUM(round_number)

examples.prompt: How many rounds were played in this series in total?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: round count → the rounds table, one row per round.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rounds WHERE series_id = ?")
Use COUNT(*); if you use round_number, you may only take MAX as the highest round number — you must not sum it.

typical_misconceptions: Using SUM(round_number) as 'how many rounds were played' —— that sums round numbers, so the unit of measure is completely wrong

topics.name: map game grain (games)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: One game = the rounds played on a single map; the round table sits one level below it

skills: One row of games = one game on one map (game_id ↔ series_id + map_name)
Cross-map comparison must group by game — you cannot simply average over all rounds

examples.prompt: Which maps were played in this series?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: maps → the games table (DISTINCT map_name on rounds also works, but only game_id carries the game identity).
MCP: query_sql("SELECT game_id, map_name FROM games WHERE series_id = ?")

typical_misconceptions: Pooling the rounds of all maps together to compute 'the win rate on this map' —— you must first split by game_id or map_name

topics.name: series grain (series)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: One series = several games (BO3/BO5); games sit one level below it

skills: One row of series = one series, and it is the entry parameter for the vast majority of reporting tools

examples.prompt: Give me an overview of this match.
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: series level → reporting tools all take series_id as their entry point.
MCP: match_summary_report(series_id=?) —— look at the overview first, then decide which layer to drill into.

typical_misconceptions: Using a series-level summary to answer a round-level question ('who won round 7' is not in the series table)

topics.name: tournament grain (agg_tournament_stats)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Tournament-level summaries roll up from series

skills: The grain of agg_tournament_stats is (tournament_id, entity_type, entity_id)

examples.prompt: How did this team perform overall in this tournament?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: across series → the tournament layer.
MCP: scouting_report(team_name=?, last_n_series=5) —— a profile across series.

typical_misconceptions: A tournament-level win rate is not the same as a series-level win rate —— rolling up discards information about how strong the opponents were

topics.name: round outcome and win type
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: The win/loss outcome is recorded on the round row

related.reason: Losing streaks / winning streaks are consecutive runs in the sequence of round outcomes

skills: winning_team_name is a column of the round row; reading it tells you who won the round
win_type distinguishes elimination / spike detonation / defusal / time-out

examples.prompt: How many rounds did each team win in this series?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: round level → rounds.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT winning_team_name, COUNT(*) FROM rounds WHERE series_id = ? GROUP BY winning_team_name")
The denominator is **all** rounds; do not put winning_team_name in the WHERE clause, otherwise the win rate is always 100%.

examples.prompt: What happened between round 7 and round 12?
answer_outline: MCP: match_rounds_report(series_id=?, round_start=7, round_end=12) —— a round-by-round timeline.

typical_misconceptions: Putting winning_team_name in the WHERE clause and then computing a 'win rate' —— the denominator has been filtered away by your own filter, so the win rate is always 100% (found in practice; call it definition self-immolation)

topics.name: first blood
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: First blood is the first kill of a round

skills: The grain of agg_first_blood_stats is round_id, one row per round
The fields fb_team (the team that took first blood) and fb_team_won (whether the first-blood side ultimately won the round)

examples.prompt: How many first bloods did Cloud9 get in this match?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: round-level first-blood facts → agg_first_blood_stats (already ordered — do not try to derive it yourself from the events).
MCP: query_sql("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agg_first_blood_stats WHERE series_id = ? AND fb_team = ?")

examples.prompt: Where do I find the first-blood related metrics for this match?
answer_outline: MCP: match_analysis_report(series_id=?, team_name=?) —— the first-blood and conversion metrics live in this report.

typical_misconceptions: Treating the first kill event in base_events as first blood —— event order is not guaranteed, so you must use agg_first_blood_stats, the already-ordered aggregate table

topics.name: first blood conversion rate
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Conversion rate = rounds where the team took first blood and won the round / rounds where it took first blood

related.reason: It is also a 'was the advantage cashed in' conversion rate, with the same definitional structure

skills: Conversion rate = AVG(fb_team_won) * 100, with the denominator being the rounds where fb_team = your team
You must report the sample size (COUNT(*)) alongside it, otherwise there is no way to tell whether the rate is stable

examples.prompt: After taking first blood in this match, what proportion of rounds did Cloud9 ultimately win?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: round level → agg_first_blood_stats.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT ROUND(AVG(fb_team_won)*100, 1) AS conv, COUNT(*) AS n FROM agg_first_blood_stats WHERE series_id = ? AND fb_team = ?")
The SQL must return exactly **one row** (it uses aggregation with no GROUP BY) —— when multiple rows come back the ground truth only takes row 0, so it drifts with row order.
Report conv together with n: if n is small you can only say 'that is how this match went'.

examples.prompt: What is the first blood conversion rate on each map separately?
answer_outline: This kind of question is inherently a **multi-value** answer; either aggregate back to a single value in an outer query, or make the ORDER BY … LIMIT 1 explicit and take one.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT ROUND(AVG(fb_team_won)*100, 1) AS conv, COUNT(*) AS n FROM agg_first_blood_stats WHERE series_id = ? AND fb_team = ? AND map_name = ?")  -- query once per map

typical_misconceptions: Putting GROUP BY map_name in the SQL without aggregating —— it returns multiple rows, the ground truth only takes row 0, and the question can then never be answered correctly (`map_fb_conv_window` was broken exactly this way in practice)
Asking for 'the conversion rate on each map' but retrieving the data as a single scalar —— either aggregate again in an outer query, or make the ORDER BY … LIMIT 1 explicit

topics.name: post-plant situation (post-plant)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: The outcome after the plant is also one form of round win/loss

skills: The grain of agg_post_plant_stats is round_id
Distinguish a detonation from a defuse —— the two possible outcomes for the attacking side

examples.prompt: After planting the spike on this map, what proportion did Cloud9 ultimately convert?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: round level → base_events (plant / defuse events) + rounds.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN event_type='plant' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS plants, COUNT(*) AS n FROM base_events WHERE map_name = ? AND actor_team_name = ? AND event_type IN ('plant','defuse')")
Do **not** GROUP BY round_id here —— that gives one 0/1 per round, whereas the question asks for the proportion across the whole map.

examples.prompt: How do the economy and tactical tempo of this match look?
answer_outline: MCP: match_economy_report(series_id=?, team_name=?)

typical_misconceptions: Writing 'per-round spike success rate' as a GROUP BY round_id —— that is one 0/1 per round, whereas what is wanted is the proportion after aggregating over the whole map (`plant_success_rate_lotus` was broken by exactly this: the ground truth took row 0 and got 100%, while the correct aggregation is 70%)
Counting a defuse as a successful plant —— you must separate the event types first

topics.name: economy and equipment choices
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Economic state is recorded at the round/team level

related.reason: Losing streaks often come with an economy collapse

skills: agg_team_round_stats carries the equipment value and what survives for that round

examples.prompt: What is the economy trend and the attacking patterns in this match?
answer_outline: MCP: match_economy_report(series_id=?, team_name=?)

typical_misconceptions: Treating 'pistol round' as a fixed round number —— a pistol round is round 1 of each half, not round 1 of the whole match

topics.name: clutch situations (clutch)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: A clutch is a special case of a round win/loss

skills: A clutch = winning a round while outnumbered; the flag lives in agg_player_round_stats

examples.prompt: Which highlight rounds (clutches) happened in this match?
answer_outline: MCP: match_players_report(series_id=?, team_name=?) —— the highlight rounds are in this report.

typical_misconceptions: Treating 'the last surviving teammate' as a clutch —— it only counts when the opponents are more numerous

topics.name: trades (trade)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: A trade happens within the time window after first blood

skills: A trade has a strict time window — you cannot count 'everyone died during the round' as a trade

examples.prompt: How efficient is this team at trading?
answer_outline: MCP: match_analysis_report(series_id=?, team_name=?)

typical_misconceptions: Ignoring the time window and counting every death in the round as a trade

topics.name: map pool win rate
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Map win rates are aggregated per game

skills: The grain of agg_team_map_stats is (team_name, map_name, tournament_name)

examples.prompt: How has this team performed on each map?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: the map pool across tournaments → agg_team_map_stats.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT map_name, wins, losses FROM agg_team_map_stats WHERE team_name = ?")
With a sample of only 1 game you can only say 'that is how this game went', not 'this is a strong map'.

typical_misconceptions: Taking a single map from one series and declaring it 'a strong map' —— the sample size is just 1 game, which cannot support a conclusion

topics.name: attack and defend halves
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Halves are split by round number

related.reason: Split attack and defense apart first, then compute the round conversion rate for each side

skills: Halves are split by round_number (first half / overtime counted separately), and the attack and defense roles swap at the side switch

examples.prompt: How did each half of this map play out?
answer_outline: MCP: match_rounds_report(series_id=?, map_name=?) —— includes the half split.

typical_misconceptions: Judging attack/defense by whether the round number is odd or even —— the side switch happens at half-time, it does not alternate

topics.name: round conversion rate by side
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: You can only have a side win rate once you have split the sides

skills: Side win rate = rounds won by that side / total rounds for that side

examples.prompt: On this map, how many rounds did Cloud9 win as the attacking side?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: round level + side → rounds (with side / winning_team_name).
MCP: query_sql("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rounds WHERE series_id = ? AND map_name = ? AND side = ? AND winning_team_name = ?")
The denominator must be the total rounds of **that side**, not the total rounds of the whole map.

typical_misconceptions: Using the win rate across the whole map as the attacking-side win rate —— the baselines of the two sides differ a lot

topics.name: KAST
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: KAST is recorded at the (game_id, player_id) level

skills: KAST = the share of rounds with a kill / assist / survival / being traded
Both agg_player_game_stats and agg_player_series_stats exist, at different grains

examples.prompt: What is this player's KAST on this map?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: a single map → agg_player_game_stats (not the series table).
MCP: query_sql("SELECT player_name, kast_percentage FROM agg_player_game_stats WHERE game_id = ?")
First confirm whether it is stored as a ratio (0.78) or a percentage (78) —— both conventions have been observed in practice.

typical_misconceptions: Reading a value of 0.78 in kast_percentage as 78 —— what is stored is a ratio, not a percentage, so you must confirm the convention first
Writing the column name from memory (kast_pct) —— the actual column is kast_percentage, and a wrong name fails immediately with a Binder Error
Using a series-level KAST to answer 'what was his KAST on this map' —— a grain mismatch

topics.name: ADR (average damage per round)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: ADR is recorded at the (game_id, player_id) level

related.reason: KAST and ADR are often looked at together, but their units of measure differ

skills: The denominator of ADR is the round count, not the kill count

examples.prompt: How has this player's ADR trended over their recent games?
answer_outline: MCP: player_profile_report(player_name=?, last_n_series=5)

typical_misconceptions: Reading ADR as total damage —— it is an average per round

topics.name: K/D and the differential
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: K/D is recorded at the (game_id, player_id) level

skills: Tell kills/deaths (a ratio) apart from kills-deaths (a differential)

examples.prompt: How do the players of the two teams compare in this match?
answer_outline: MCP: match_players_report(series_id=?, team_name=?)

typical_misconceptions: Reporting the K/D differential as if it were the ratio

topics.name: opening duels (opening duel)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Opening duels produce first blood

skills: Tell 'participated in an opening duel' apart from 'took first blood' —— there is a losing side

examples.prompt: How does this team fare in opening duels?
answer_outline: MCP: match_analysis_report(series_id=?, team_name=?)

typical_misconceptions: Reading the opening-duel participation rate as the first blood rate

topics.name: Win Shares (contribution share)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Win Shares is a weighted combination of several base metrics
Damage is one of the weights

skills: The grain of agg_player_win_shares is (player_id, game_id), and the weights come from ref_win_probability_factors

examples.prompt: What is each player's contribution (Win Shares) in this match?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: (player_id, game_id) → agg_player_win_shares.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT * FROM agg_player_win_shares WHERE game_id = ?")
State that this is a **derived value** computed with VCT Americas 2025 weights, not official data.

typical_misconceptions: Treating Win Shares as official data —— it is a derived value computed with VCT Americas 2025 weights

topics.name: player consistency (variation across games)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Consistency means looking at the distribution of the same metric across multiple games

skills: Cross-game comparison requires the variance/range, not just comparing means

examples.prompt: Is this player performing consistently?
answer_outline: MCP: player_profile_report(player_name=?, last_n_series=5, map_name=?)
Take the same metric across multiple series and look at the range and the variation, not just the mean.

typical_misconceptions: Using a player's single best game to represent their level

topics.name: agents and roles
topics.subject: valorant

related.reason: Different roles make player stats differently comparable

skills: agent_roles is a reference table: one role per agent (duelist / initiator / controller / sentinel)

examples.prompt: What role does this agent play?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: a reference table → agent_roles.
MCP: query_sql("SELECT * FROM agent_roles")

typical_misconceptions: Comparing the individual stats of different agents by role —— the roles have different duties, so a side-by-side comparison is unfair

topics.name: team performance across a series
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: The series-level team table

skills: The grain of agg_team_series_stats is (series_id, team_name)

examples.prompt: How do the two teams compare overall in this match?
answer_outline: MCP: match_summary_report(series_id=?, team_name=?)

typical_misconceptions: Using a team aggregate as if it were player data

topics.name: losing / winning streaks (streak)
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: A losing streak is a consecutive run in the sequence of round outcomes

related.reason: After a losing streak you normally check whether the momentum carries over

skills: gaps-and-islands：subtract two ROW_NUMBER() values to get the island id, then group by that id and count
The filter must come **after** the numbering, otherwise the whole run is treated as a single block
The start of the longest run is the MIN **within that run**, not the MIN of the whole group

examples.prompt: Cloud9's longest losing streak on this map is how many rounds long, and which round does it start from?
answer_outline: Confirm the grain: the round sequence → rounds, and it must be **ordered by round number**.

MCP: query_sql("SELECT cnt AS max_streak, start_round FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt, MIN(round_number) AS start_round FROM (SELECT round_number, losing_team_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY round_number) AS rn, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY losing_team_name ORDER BY round_number) AS grp FROM rounds WHERE series_id = ? AND map_name = ?) t WHERE losing_team_name = ? GROUP BY (rn - grp)) x ORDER BY cnt DESC, start_round ASC LIMIT 1")
The three steps cannot be reordered: number the whole sequence first → then filter to the target team → then group by (rn-grp).
The trailing ORDER BY … LIMIT 1 guarantees a single returned row (a unique ground truth).

typical_misconceptions: Using COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY round_number) as the 'longest losing streak' —— that is a running count, not the length of a consecutive run
Filtering before numbering —— the island ids merge into one block and the result comes out too large (13 instead of 8 was observed in practice)
Taking MIN(round_number) directly as the start —— that gives the smallest round number of the whole group, not the longest run (R1 instead of R7 was observed in practice)

topics.name: momentum
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Momentum is the interpretation layered on top of a consecutive run

skills: Momentum requires looking at both the length of the run and whether it was later broken; the run length alone misleads

examples.prompt: Has this team picked up momentum?
answer_outline: MCP: match_rounds_report(series_id=?, map_name=?)
Look at the run length plus whether it was broken afterwards; a run of 3 rounds or fewer is not enough to read momentum.

typical_misconceptions: Calling 'winning 3 rounds in a row' momentum —— a 3-round sample is not enough to interpret

topics.name: opponent scouting
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Scouting spans multiple series

skills: A scouting report must aggregate across series; a single match is not convincing

examples.prompt: What style does the next opponent play?
answer_outline: MCP: scouting_report(team_name=?, last_n_series=5, map_name=?)
Give last_n_series at least 5; a single match only shows how that one match went.

typical_misconceptions: Scouting an opponent from a single match —— that is the state of that match, not a stable trait of the opponent

topics.name: cross-dataset pattern detection
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Pattern detection is scouting at scale

skills: pattern_detection_report has a min_rounds threshold and returns no conclusion when the sample is too small

examples.prompt: Which patterns does this team keep repeating?
answer_outline: MCP: pattern_detection_report(team_name=?, min_rounds=200)
Check the sample size first: when the round count is below min_rounds the conclusion is not trustworthy (the current database has only 59 rounds).

typical_misconceptions: Running pattern detection on 59 rounds of data —— that is below min_rounds, so the conclusion is not trustworthy

topics.name: grain traps
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: You have to separate the grains before metrics even make sense

related.reason: Series-level KAST and single-map KAST are often conflated
Per-map and whole-match first blood conversion rates are often conflated

skills: Before answering, state it explicitly: is the grain of this question a round / a game / a series / a tournament? Which table does it map to?

examples.prompt: I'm not sure which table this question should query.
answer_outline: MCP: get_database_info() —— check the grain and row count of every table first.
Pick the table by the grain of the question: rounds → rounds / agg_*_round_*; a single map → games / agg_*_game_*; series → series / agg_*_series_*; tournament → agg_tournament_stats.

typical_misconceptions: Using an aggregate table to answer a detail-level question (or the other way round)
Adding across grains: adding a round-level count directly to a game-level count

topics.name: sample size and conclusion strength
topics.subject: valorant

prerequisites.reason: Get the grain right first, and only then ask whether the sample is large enough

skills: Reporting a ratio means you must also report the denominator; when the denominator is small you can only say 'that is how this match went', not 'that is who they are'

examples.prompt: What is Cloud9's first blood conversion rate? Is that conclusion solid?
answer_outline: MCP: query_sql("SELECT ROUND(AVG(fb_team_won)*100, 1) AS conv, COUNT(*) AS n FROM agg_first_blood_stats WHERE series_id = ? AND fb_team = ?")
Report the value (conv) and the sample size (n) **together**; if n is small, scope the conclusion to this one series.

typical_misconceptions: Reporting only the percentage and omitting the sample size
